conflicts.description: The same movie/title entity is named title_basics in the IMDB schema and film in the Sakila schema; film_text is a denormalized duplicate of the same concept.
conflicts.resolution: Merged under a single resource named title, absorbing film_text as a denormalized duplicate.

conflicts.description: The same person entity is called name_basics in IMDB and actor in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Merged under a single resource named person.

conflicts.description: Title identifiers (tconst vs film_id) and person identifiers (nconst vs actor_id) use different column names for the same identity.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to neutral title_id and person_id respectively.

conflicts.description: Equivalent attributes carry divergent names across schemas (startyear/release_year, runtimeminutes/length, primarytitle/title).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to release_year, runtime_minutes and primary_title.

conflicts.description: The film classification taxonomy is named category in Sakila and genres in IMDB.
conflicts.resolution: Unified as genre with a shared name attribute.

conflicts.description: The token rating is a homonym: in IMDB it denotes a numeric user score, in Sakila it denotes an MPAA-style content rating.
conflicts.resolution: Disambiguated into separate attributes average_rating (numeric score) and content_rating (age/classification rating).

conflicts.description: IMDB models identifiers as number while Sakila models them as string (and some Sakila FK columns as integer).
conflicts.resolution: All identifiers standardized to string, since IMDB identifiers are alphanumeric and references must match.

conflicts.description: Runtime is typed as string in film.length but integer in title_basics.runtimeminutes.
conflicts.resolution: Cast to integer runtime_minutes (values expressed in minutes).

conflicts.description: All year attributes are typed as string in the sources, using a null sentinel for missing values.
conflicts.resolution: Converted to integer, mapping the null sentinel to null.

conflicts.description: Boolean flags are represented as string in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Converted to boolean.

conflicts.description: Monetary values are typed as string in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Converted to number.

conflicts.description: Date-time values are typed as date despite descriptions stating date and time.
conflicts.resolution: Typed as datetime to preserve the time component; pure date columns (last_update, create_date) remain date.

conflicts.description: title_basics.primarytitle is typed as integer although it holds textual title content.
conflicts.resolution: Corrected to string.

conflicts.description: Boolean attributes are documented as 0/1 integer codes.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to boolean.

conflicts.description: Language is encoded as an ISO code in title_akas.language but as an English name in sakila.language.name; different encodings of the same dimension.
conflicts.resolution: Sakila retains language_id/name as the canonical language dimension; the IMDB alias language is kept as a distinct language_code attribute to avoid conflating code and name.

conflicts.description: The two genre/category taxonomies use overlapping but non-identical value sets (e.g. IMDB Drama vs Sakila Classics).
conflicts.resolution: Merged into a single genre dimension matched by name, accepting that the combined value space is broader than either source.

conflicts.description: Boolean semantics are encoded inconsistently (0/1 integers vs TRUE/FALSE strings).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to a single boolean representation with true/false semantics.

conflicts.description: Both measure duration; IMDB uses an explicit minutes unit in the name, Sakila an implicit one.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as runtime_minutes with an explicit, consistent minutes unit.

conflicts.description: Missing values are encoded with a string sentinel in the IMDB year columns.
conflicts.resolution: Sentinel values reinterpreted as null in numeric target columns.

conflicts.description: Person-title involvement is modeled three different ways: multi-valued arrays (title_crew.directors/writers), an attributed credit table (title_principals with category/job/characters), and a plain junction table (film_actor).
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into a single title_credit resource capturing person, title, role, job and characters; crew arrays are exploded into one row per person with a fixed role.

conflicts.description: Genres are a multi-valued column in IMDB but a fully normalized many-to-many structure in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into genre plus a title_genre junction table.

conflicts.description: A person notable titles are stored as an array of title identifiers.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into the person_known_for_title junction table.

conflicts.description: A person professions are stored as an array of strings.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into the person_profession child table.

conflicts.description: film_text denormalizes film title and description into a separate search table.
conflicts.resolution: Folded into the title resource; the duplicate columns were mapped onto the same target attributes.

conflicts.description: Episode relationships and ratings are held in separate 1:1 side tables in IMDB rather than embedded attributes.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as dedicated title_episode and title_rating resources to keep the title entity normalized.

conflicts.description: Person names are stored as a single unsplit string in IMDB but split into first/last components in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Retained both representations (primary_name and first_name/last_name) to preserve information from either source.

conflicts.description: Title-to-genre is N:M in Sakila (junction table) but an unbounded multi-value field in IMDB.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as an N:M relationship via the title_genre junction table.

conflicts.description: Person-to-title involvement is N:M across all sources.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as an N:M relationship via the title_credit table.

conflicts.description: A title has many alternative titles (1:N).
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as a 1:N child resource title_aka keyed by (title_id, ordering).

conflicts.description: A TV series has many episodes (1:N self-referencing relationship).
conflicts.resolution: Preserved via title_episode with title_id and parent_title_id both referencing title.

conflicts.description: Ratings relate to a title 1:1.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as a 1:1 side table title_rating keyed by title_id.

conflicts.description: Persons and their known-for titles form an N:M relationship.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as N:M via person_known_for_title.

conflicts.description: title_akas declares no primary key, though (titleid, ordering) uniquely identifies rows.
conflicts.resolution: Composite primary key defined as (title_id, ordering).

conflicts.description: Several source resources declare no primary key, leaving their identity ambiguous.
conflicts.resolution: Natural/composite keys were assigned where derivable (title_episode.title_id, title_rating.title_id, title_genre composite, title_aka composite) and a synthetic surrogate credit_id was introduced for title_credit.

conflicts.description: IMDB uses a natural alphanumeric key (tconst) while Sakila uses a surrogate key (film_id) for the same title entity.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into title_id whose provenance lists both source keys.

conflicts.description: IMDB uses a natural key (nconst) while Sakila uses a surrogate key (actor_id) for the same person entity.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into person_id whose provenance lists both source keys.

conflicts.description: film_text.film_id is a de facto foreign key to film but no foreign key is declared.
conflicts.resolution: Treated as an alias of the title identifier and folded into title_id.
